title: Fit each course to its grade and test
statement: Set a course's passage lengths, genre mix and demands from its own grade and test, building toward that test's reading load, rather than porting a sibling course's harder texts.
example: One course's practice passages ran 58 to 217 words where its test presents about 2,740 across several passages.
detail: The course plans' rejection lessons record that a third-grade course's passages ran 58–217 words when the test is multi-passage at about 2,740 words, so length has to ramp toward test stamina, and that its texts were flagged at about 22% literary against a target of about 40% because they were picked on Lexile alone, so genre balance is a design commitment, not a backfill (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`). Their grade-band register requires a course to be demonstrably different from its siblings on text band, stamina, genre split, item formats, rigor, gate design and other dimensions, with grade-specific sources (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`), and a rule from a seventh-grade BrainLift differentiates adjacent grades by the knowledge and operation learners must master rather than cloning a sibling course with harder text (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/sources/review-hub/course-insights-d7f57fb/ATOMS.json`, RHBL-023). Its reading lengthens from the start toward the test's load, long and paired passages included, because short passages alone do not build sustained reading.
against: The same register still marks the stamina rows for grades 2 to 5 [TO SOURCE], so the target lengths themselves are not yet set (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`). The evidence is one course's gap; nothing here measures what longer passages did for scores.
